title: Summit and Wreck
premise: Rosalind Blackwood's estranged father, salvage magnate Edmund Blackwood, vanishes upriver chasing the wreck of the Meridian Star—a colonial-era treasure ship whose manifest he believes names him as heir to a fortune built on his own family's betrayal. When his expedition goes silent, Rosalind takes a charter from his ruthless business partner Vane, who wants the wreck found first and witnesses left behind. Racing the monsoon and six falling tides, she discovers her father alive but broken by what he learned: the inheritance is real, and it was stolen. In the climax at the wreck itself, Rosalind must choose between salvaging the proof that would ruin Vane and saving her father as the river floods; she chooses him, letting the evidence sink, and returns with something better—an identity no longer defined by what she's owed.
about_author: Lior Eastwick is a former deckhand on cargo barges who spent a decade mapping tributaries of Southeast Asian rivers before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for water-soaked prose and protagonists who trust rivers more than people.

chapters.title: The Silence Above the Bend
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Running her riverboat through low-water season, Rosalind receives a garbled distress call from her father's expedition, then a visit from Vane offering triple pay to 'rescue' it. She distrusts him but needs the money—and answers about the father who abandoned her. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment, old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, intercut with journal fragments from her father. Navigating hostile rapids and a sabotaged radio relay, she realizes Vane's crew is armed and his charts mark the wreck too precisely—he always knew where it was. A crew member defects and confesses Vane plans no rescue. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve; the race becomes real.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She reaches the wreck ahead of Vane by shooting an uncharted channel during a spring tide, finding her father half-mad in a cave with the Meridian Star's manifest—proof the Blackwood fortune was plundered and its rightful heirs erased. Vane arrives; monsoon clouds swallow the horizon. Emotional beat: revelation and confrontation, truth versus survival.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. With the river rising, Rosalind must load either the manifest or her injured father onto her overloaded boat—not both. She burns the papers to light their escape downriver through the flood, outmaneuvering Vane, whose greed strands him when his own vessel founders. Home again, she claims no fortune but her own name. Emotional beat: sacrifice, release, hard-won peace.
